Our research bot read three point five hours as thirty-five.
By the time anyone noticed, it was in the blog, the landing page, a Short, and a waitlist email.
So we put every claim our bots make into a FalkorDB graph.
Green nodes are sources. Purple are the claims quoted from them. Blue is everything our bots built on top.
First, a QA agent checks receipts. The number has to appear in the quote it cites. Thirty-five doesn't. And ten thousand teams has no source at all.
Now one correction. FalkorDB walks every derived-from path, at any depth. Ten artifacts, up to four hops away, turn red in one query.
And the FAQ stays clean. It never touched that claim. No path means no taint. That's proof, not a guess.
So, why is the Short wrong? The graph answers with the whole chain: the Short, the script, the blog, the brief, the bad claim, and the exact source line.
Each fix goes back to the bot that made it, as a redo task. Their next step comes straight from the graph.
Every agent also earns a trust score, computed from its own track record of claims.
It's a handful of Cypher queries, exposed over MCP, so any agent can read and write it.
Taint plus Receipts. One wrong number. Every place it spread.
